subject: Optimize Toolkit: Finlytics pilot economics & quant/caching guidance
messages:
From: Elena Varela <elena.varela@finlytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot ask: Optimize toolkit recommendations + pricing

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the product overview last week — we liked the Optimize ideas around batching and caching. Before we get the PO process moving, procurement asked for a concise pricing path and what kind of recommendations you would provide for quantization and cache TTL for our use case.

Quick context: Finlytics is building a compliance review assistant that will process short documents (avg 400 tokens) and run frequent lookups for policy snippets. Expected steady-state: ~600k tokens/day with spikes to ~2M tokens/day during batch runs. Latency sensitivity is moderate (tail P95 target < 350ms).

Can you send:
- A simple pilot offer (credits/discounts) for a 60-day POC
- Your recommended quantization choices (safety/quality tradeoffs) and caching best-practices for policy snippet reuse
- Any constraints around persisted caches for compliance/auditability

Attaching our usage snapshot and a sample anonymized extract. Happy to hop on a short call if needed.

Thanks,
Elena

--
Elena Varela
Head of AI Products, Finlytics
elena.varela@finlytics.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Varela <elena.varela@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: Optimize toolkit recommendations + pricing

Thanks for the detail, Elena — helpful context. I've looped in Marissa (sales lead) and Aditya (solutions) to make sure we cover both commercial and technical sides. High-level reply to get this moving:

1) Pilot offer (60 days) – high level
- 200k free token credits for model inference (usable across text-gen + embeddings)
- 20% off incremental consumption during pilot
- Option to convert credits into a committed starter tier if you go into production within 90 days

2) Quantization recommendation
- Start with 8-bit (int8 / 4-bit quantization techniques vary by model family). Most open-architecture models we recommend: 8-bit for parity on quality with ~2.4x cost reduction.
- Move to 4-bit for latency-sensitive, high-throughput paths after validating output quality on your eval set. We provide a quant-eval harness to measure regressions per prompt set.

3) Caching guidance
- Prefix caching for policy snippets: use a short TTL (24–72h) if snippets change frequently; consider explicit invalidation hooks when policy updates are pushed.
- For deterministic lookups (exact-match policy retrieval), use our KV caching with a cold-start warmup and optional persistent backing (encrypted).
- Cache scope: we can configure session-scoped vs account-wide caches; for compliance, account-wide with audit logs is typical.

4) Compliance note on persisted cache
- Persistent caches are encrypted at rest and appear in audit logs. We can enable key rotations and exportable audit trails if your security team requires them.

Next steps I propose: Aditya will draft a short technical appendix describing quant eval steps + batching windows we recommend for your token distribution, and Marissa will prepare a one-page commercial summary that maps to the pilot credits above. If that looks good we can follow up with a formal quote and DocuSign link.

Would you like us to include an SLA paragraph for pilot operations?

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.inference

Subject: Re: Pilot ask: Pilot commercial options + packaging

Elena — adding a few practical options so procurement has something to sign off on quickly.

Commercial packaging options (clear, pick one):
- Option A — Evaluation (no commitment): 200k credits + 20% off per-token for 60 days. No SLA.
- Option B — Starter commit: $10k/month committed for 3 months (applied as credits), includes 10% committed discount and 2 business-day support SLA.
- Option C — Pilot-to-Prod bundle: $25k one-time pilot package (includes credits + implementation support), converts to committed T&M discount schedule on signature within 90 days.

Discount flex: For mid-sized commitments (>$50k ARR expected), we can layer an efficiency incentive tied to measurable cost-per-1k tokens improvements (quant + batching adoption).

On the technical side: recommended batching window to meet P95 <350ms for your profile is 20–50ms with adaptive batching; Aditya will validate against your usage snapshot.

If procurement needs standard terms, we'll send the one-pager + standard MSA snippet.

-Marissa

Thanks — that framing is very helpful. A few clarifying points from procurement & infra:
- We expect the 2M token/day spikes to last 6–8 hours at month-end.
- For compliance we need: exportable audit logs for cache invalidation events, and a retention policy of 365 days for those logs.
- Can you confirm whether persistent caches are stored in our VPC (for Private deployment) or in Redwood-managed storage for hosted pilots?

Procurement also asked whether the pilot SLA (if included) would cover incident response for degraded latency during spikes, or only platform availability.

If you can confirm, we can fast-track Option B (starter commit).

Best,
Elena
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Varela <elena.varela@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: Pilot commercial options + packaging

Elena — quick answers inline: 

- Spike handling: our Starter commit includes a burst buffer for short spikes (up to 2x committed throughput for <8 hours/day). For sustained spikes beyond that we’d discuss temporary add-on capacity. The pilot 20% off incremental consumption applies during the 60 days.

- Persistent cache location: for hosted pilots, cache backing is Redwood-managed encrypted storage; for Private deployments we can configure cache persistence into your VPC. Given your compliance needs, we recommend a short Private deployment for the pilot (customer-managed storage) — that lets you control key management and audit exports.

- Audit logs & retention: we can export cache invalidation events and request-level logs to a secure S3 bucket in your account (or an SFTP endpoint) with retention policies you control. We will surface a daily audit snapshot during the pilot and include an exportable log for procurement review.

- SLA scope for Starter commit: 2 business-day response for incidents; operational latency degradations during spikes are covered by our incident response team but do not constitute an SLA breach unless they cross the defined availability thresholds. We can discuss an elevated response SLA as an add-on.

I've attached a one-page pilot proposal and your usage snapshot for reference. If procurement wants Option B, I'll send a formal quote and DocuSign link (we can pre-fill procurement contact).

Next: Aditya — can you attach the quant-eval checklist and a short sim showing 8-bit vs 4-bit quality delta for the sample prompts Elena provided?

Thanks,
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee

soojin_lee@redwood.inference
